title: Strict quotient-system representative of one normalized DVR tower
statement: Let l be a prime, E a finite-dimensional field extension of Padic l, X a scheme, D a finite-field datum, and hl : l ≠ D.p. Let T be a normalized DVR tower [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. There is a cochain complex Q over the quotient ringed sequence site [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], with isomorphisms a_n : T.M n ≅ ev_n(Q), such that tau_(m,n) followed by Res(a_n) equals a_m followed by the quotient-system transition for every n ≤ m. Moreover T.tower is isomorphic, in the derived category of strict completed-coefficient towers, to the completed scalar restriction of Q. No Hom comparison is asserted. The coefficient-derived functors and localization are precisely those in the attached Lean statement.

source.place: Second proof paragraph: finite mapping-complex comparisons and reduction-compatible counits.

proof.text: Apply the canonical constant-tower Roos theorem to T.tower. Its specified total limit M and product of canonical projections satisfy the Roos triangle. Normalized DVR effectivity gives invertible finite counit comparisons c_n from the derived scalar extensions of M to T.M n, with its all-quotient transition equation.

Take the derived coefficient-system reduction N of M from the coefficient evaluation calculus. The Roos triangle makes adjacent canonical projections compatible; induct on the larger index, using localization of evaluation identity and composition, to obtain compatibility for every n <= m. Compose with the canonical restricted-evaluation isomorphisms. The reduction adjunction unit-projection formula and the finite adjunction Hom equivalence identify the transition of N with the canonical reduction transition. Compose the inverses of c_n with the finite reduction-evaluation isomorphisms; the two canonical transition equations imply compatibility of these finite isomorphisms b_n.

Choose a cochain complex Q representing N via essential surjectivity of the derived localization. Transport b_n along its localization isomorphism; naturality of the localized quotient transitions gives the asserted all-pair equations for a_n. This is only the representative of the already constructed quotient-system object, not an arbitrary witness used in a definition.

Compose T.evaluationIso with completed scalar restriction of a_n and the inverse canonical restricted-evaluation isomorphism. The restricted-transition square and T.tower_tau make this family commute with successor transitions. Sequential tower evaluation fullness supplies a morphism realizing this fixed family. Each evaluated morphism is an isomorphism; exact evaluation commutes with derived homology, so each homology map is componentwise invertible and hence invertible as a natural transformation. The derived isomorphism criterion makes the lifted morphism an isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem normalizedDVR_quotient_system_realization
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (T : NormalizedDVRTower l E X D hl) :
    ∃ (Q : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l E X) ℤ)
      (a : ∀ n : ℕ, T.M n ≅
        (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E X n).obj (coefTraceInput l E X Q)),
      (∀ {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m),
        T.tau h ≫ (normalizedDVRRes l E X h).map (a n).hom =
          (a m).hom ≫ (coefficientSequenceDerivedTransition l E X h).app
            (coefTraceInput l E X Q)) ∧
      Nonempty (T.tower ≅ (coefficientSequenceDerivedRestriction l E X).obj
        (coefTraceInput l E X Q))
